spec.problem: `messageTime` in `src/lib/chat/time.ts:10` decides between "Today", "Yesterday" and a weekday by counting whole 24-hour periods since the message: `Math.floor((now - at) / DAY)`. It does not count calendar days. A message sent at 11:50 PM and viewed at 12:10 AM is 20 minutes old, so `days` is 0 and it shows "Today", even though it was yesterday. In the same way, a message from late evening two days ago, viewed the next morning, is less than 48 hours old, so `days` is 1 and it shows "Yesterday" instead of its weekday. The weekday-or-date cutoff at line 23 (`days < 7`) is off by the same amount. The fix is to compare the local calendar dates of `at` and `now`. Take each one's local midnight and divide the difference by `DAY`, rounding to the nearest whole number so that 23-hour and 25-hour daylight-saving days still count as one day. The label is built in `src/components/message.tsx:91`, which only calls this function.

(2) Viewed at Tue 6 Oct 08:00, a message from Sun 4 Oct 23:00 is expected to show /^Sunday 11:00\sPM$/; the current code gives Yesterday. spec.problem:
When another tab saves, `App.tsx:141-164` dispatches `{ type: "sync", incoming, keepChatId }`. The reducer's `sync` case (`src/lib/chat/store.ts:100-106`) merges the two lists by id: it starts from the incoming chats and then overwrites them with every local chat (`for (const c of state.chats) byId.set(c.id, c)`). That causes both symptoms in the issue.
1. Deleted chats come back. A chat deleted in tab 1 is missing from `incoming` but still in tab 2's state, so the merge keeps it. The next time tab 2 saves (any later action, `App.tsx:167-178`), the chat is written back to localStorage, and tab 1 gets it back through its own sync.
2. New messages don't show up. If tab 2 already has the chat open, its own copy wins the conflict, so the new messages from tab 1 are dropped. Tab 2's next save then overwrites them in storage too.
The comment at line 101 says "ours win on conflicts, so nothing in progress is lost". But only one local chat can be in progress: the one passed as `keepChatId`, which the reducer currently ignores. Every other local chat is already saved (the persist effect writes after each change unless an answer is being generated), so `incoming` is the up-to-date copy of all the others.

files.why: Make the sync case treat the other tab's saved state as the truth: take its chats as they are, keep only the local copy of the chat this tab is still writing into (keepChatId), and keep this tab's activeId only if that chat still exists. Update the comment on the action type to match.

(2) local has chat a with one message, incoming has chat a with an extra message, keepChatId null: the result must use the incoming messages. (3) the active chat is deleted in incoming: activeId falls back to the first remaining chat. The two existing sync tests must keep passing.

Rewrite the `sync` case in src/lib/chat/store.ts so incoming wins, except for the keepChatId chat, and activeId falls back when its chat is gone.

spec.problem: Assistant replies are rendered with react-markdown in `src/components/message.tsx:55`, and the only override is for `a` (lines 13-19). Image syntax `![alt](https://host/x.png)` therefore becomes a real ``, and the browser fetches it from that host as soon as the message renders, with no click needed. Model output is untrusted, so a reply can make the browser contact any server, and the URL can carry text from the chat. In production the CSP in `vite.config.ts:19` (`img-src 'self' data: blob:`) blocks the load. `pnpm dev` sends no CSP (`vite.config.ts:33,87`, only the isolation headers), so the request goes out, which is what the reporter saw. Even in production the privacy claim should not depend on the CSP alone, because the CSP is described as a backstop (`vite.config.ts:9-12`). The fake engine repeats the user message back ("Fake answer to: ", `src/lib/engine/fake-worker.ts:46`), so the bug can be reproduced in Playwright without a model.
